title: The colloquy: six lenses round one table

data.source: The twelve colloquy papers in library/colloquy/ and the lab outputs in library/colloquy/lab/, written tonight by museum workers. Counted here; not interpreted.

phoenix_quoted: MATHEMATICS.md section VII, status ONTOLOGY: "the user's Growing Block view says actual history accumulates, the present is an empty boundary carrying conditions inherited from that history, and future content is not actual." README.md: the commitments M1 to M7 "are ontology; no pre-registered test has put one at risk ("intact because it has not been tested")"; "five ontological comparisons are recorded NOT DECIDABLE". MATHEMATICS.md section II: "A rotor cut is local; the Growing Block's boundary of now would exist between cuts as well."
prediction: There are twelve papers, two from each of six lenses, and the lab outputs record at least five of the lenses' own predictions as failed. (A count written down by a rapporteur who had already read them; not a blind prediction.)
baseline: A plain count of files and of true-or-false values. Nothing here is compared with a rival theory, because nothing here tests one.
why: This book is a record of a discussion about an ontology that Phoenix itself files as not decidable. The script can count the papers and the failures the lenses recorded. It cannot check that the summary is fair, and six papers by one kind of model in one night are not evidence about the world.
claim_kind: philosophical correspondence (ONTOLOGY); a record of a discussion
would_make_it_testable: The owner's answers to the questions in colloquy/QUESTIONS_FOR_THE_OWNER.md, and then tests frozen under the protocol: a metered rate-invariance test, and a forgery or scrub experiment for what crosses a cut. The growing block itself has no test that anyone in the colloquy could name.

forks.what: two rules for what counts as a recorded prediction: the strict one in the docstring, and any true-or-false value

second_check: none: one rapporteur of the same kind of model as the six lenses; not checked by a person
